We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identities $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ and $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{cot}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x-x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
